highlights: Documented from 1124 as a fief of the Erberia family under the bishop-counts of Luni
Family seat of the Malaspina since the early 14th century, still owned by their descendants, the Marquises Torrigiani-Malaspina
Today a museum, contemporary art center, and artist/writer retreat, alongside its small B&B
description:
Castello Malaspina di Fosdinovo dates to the second half of the 12th century and rises in northern Tuscany, between the Apuan Alps and the Tyrrhenian coast. Records of its existence trace back to 1124, when it was a fief of the Erberia family under the bishop-counts of Luni, until 1317, when Spinetta Malaspina took possession of the castle. In the early 14th century, the Malaspina moved their family seat here from the nearby castle of Verrucola di Fivizzano.

Today the castle functions as a museum, a cultural center dedicated to the production and dissemination of contemporary art, a retreat for artists and writers, and houses a small bed and breakfast. The property remains in the hands of the Marquises Torrigiani-Malaspina. All the rooms are furnished with antiques, with views of the medieval village or the valley, and some feature Carrara-marble bathrooms.

The Malaspina family's continuous ownership from the early 14th century to the present, through the Torrigiani-Malaspina line, gives Fosdinovo one of the longest unbroken family tenures documented in this entire Italian collection.

The castle's dual identity as both an active museum and cultural center, alongside its small overnight accommodation, sets Fosdinovo apart from the large majority of castle-hotels in this collection, where the historic building functions primarily or exclusively as a hotel.

The artist and writer retreat program connects Fosdinovo to a specifically contemporary cultural mission, distinct from the more historically focused winery or heritage-tourism identities of most other properties here.

The surrounding Lunigiana region, the Cinque Terre, and the marble quarries of Carrara give guests staying at Fosdinovo access to a distinctive stretch of the Tuscan coast and its hinterland, less commonly featured than the Chianti or Val d'Orcia.
history: Castello Malaspina di Fosdinovo is documented from 1124 as a fief of the Erberia family under the bishop-counts of Luni, passing to Spinetta Malaspina in 1317. In the early 14th century, the Malaspina moved their family seat here, and their descendants, the Marquises Torrigiani-Malaspina, still own the property today. It functions as a museum, contemporary art center, and artist/writer retreat, alongside a small bed and breakfast within the same historic building.

faqs.question: Can I visit Fosdinovo Castle without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes — unlike most castle-hotels in this collection, Fosdinovo is an active museum and cultural center with regular guided tours open to the general public, independent of any accommodation booking.

faqs.question: Who owns Fosdinovo Castle today?
faqs.answer: The Marquises Torrigiani-Malaspina, descendants of the Malaspina family who made the castle their seat in the early 14th century.

faqs.question: Are the B&B rooms within the historic castle building?
faqs.answer: Yes — the small B&B occupies the South Wing and the "Camere dei Marchesi," all within the same historic building, furnished with antiques.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 20 minutes from La Spezia and 30 minutes from Massa by car; Pisa Airport (PSA) is about 1 hour away.

**Rooms & rates:** Rooms in the South Wing and the "Camere dei Marchesi" of the castle — including the Camera delle Bifore (the largest) and the Camera Tonda (the Marchioness's bedroom) — all within the same historic building. From €130/night.

**On-site:** Contemporary art center, artist and writer retreat, views to Portovenere and the Gulf of La Spezia from some rooms.

**Good to know:** Unlike almost all Italian castle-hotels, Fosdinovo is also an active museum with regular guided tours open to the public — worth checking visiting hours if you plan to explore beyond the accommodation area.

**Combine with:** La Spezia (~20 min), the Cinque Terre, Massa and Carrara (~30 min), the Lunigiana.
